sentences.en: And the miller's tale is essentially the same.
sentences.zh: 而磨坊主的故事本质上也一样。

sentences.en: And the miller says that he is quiting the knight, so he's paying the knight back.
sentences.zh: 磨坊主说他这是在回敬骑士，也就是说他在报复骑士。

sentences.en: And this is very disruptive.
sentences.zh: 这非常具有颠覆性。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: In the wake of the Great Revolt and the social turbulence of the age, I mean, it's a very, very bold thing for Chaucer to be doing.
sentences.zh: 在大起义和那个时代的社会动荡之后，我的意思是，对乔叟来说，这是一件非常、非常大胆的事。

sentences.en: And from that point on, the hierarchy is completely disrupted.
sentences.zh: 从那时起，等级制度彻底被打乱了。

sentences.en: So, the pilgrims are not bound by the traditional social classes.
sentences.zh: 因此，朝圣者们不再受传统社会阶层的约束。

sentences.en: Not only do you have millers, you have a merchant, a cook, a shipman, you have a lawyer, you have
sentences.zh: 不仅有磨坊主，你还有商人、厨子、船夫、律师，

sentences.en: various people from London guilds, you have a doctor, you have a yeoman who comes galloping up.
sentences.zh: 有来自伦敦各行会的各种人，有医生，还有一个骑马飞奔而来的自由民随从。

sentences.en: All kinds of things are happening all the time.
sentences.zh: 各种各样的事情一直在发生。

sentences.en: And I think that there is one of the pilgrims more than any other who embodies that sense of upheaval and novelty and, I guess, newfangledness, again, to use that Chaucerian word.
sentences.zh: 我认为，在所有的朝圣者中，有一位最能体现那种剧变、新奇感，以及我所说的“新潮感”——再次借用那个乔叟时代的词。

sentences.en: And that's probably the most famous of all the pilgrims, and that's the wife of Bath.
sentences.zh: 而她可能也是所有朝圣者中最著名的一位，那就是巴斯妇人。

sentences.en: All right.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: So, the wife of Bath, how many times has she been married?
sentences.zh: 那么，巴斯妇人，她结过几次婚？

sentences.en: Five times.
sentences.zh: 五次。

sentences.en: She's been married five times, and she tells the pilgrims that she's looking for a sixth husband.
sentences.zh: 她结过五次婚，并且她告诉朝圣者们，她正在寻找第六任丈夫。

sentences.en: Terrifying.
sentences.zh: 太可怕了。

sentences.en: Describe her to the listeners, Tom.
sentences.zh: 汤姆，向听众们描述一下她吧。

sentences.en: So, she's very handsome.
sentences.zh: 好的，她长得很漂亮。

sentences.en: She's very rosy-cheeked, although Chaucer specifies that she has a gap tooth.
sentences.zh: 她双颊红润，尽管乔叟特别提到她有点牙缝。

sentences.en: She's very broad-hipped.
sentences.zh: 她臀部很宽。

sentences.en: She wears bright red stockings.
sentences.zh: 她穿着亮红色的长袜。

sentences.en: Scandalous.
sentences.zh: 太离谱了。

sentences.en: So, very striking figure.
sentences.zh: 所以，这是一个非常引人注目的人物。

sentences.en: She's a cloth maker.
sentences.zh: 她是个织布匠。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: She is rich enough that she's a serial pilgrim.
sentences.zh: 她富有到可以算是一名职业朝圣者了。

sentences.en: So, she's been to Rome.
sentences.zh: 她去过罗马。

sentences.en: She's been to Santiago de la Compostela.
sentences.zh: 她去过圣地亚哥-德孔波斯特拉。

sentences.en: So, those are the two great pilgrimage sites in Europe.
sentences.zh: 这些是欧洲两大朝圣胜地。

sentences.en: And she's been to Jerusalem three times.
sentences.zh: 她去过耶路撒冷三次。

sentences.en: Was it possible for people to have gone multiple times to Jerusalem?
sentences.zh: 人们当时有可能多次去耶路撒冷吗？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 可以。

sentences.en: It's not beyond the bounds of possibility.
sentences.zh: 这并非完全不可能。

sentences.en: But it would be very expensive, surely.
sentences.zh: 但那肯定非常昂贵。

sentences.en: Very expensive, yes.
sentences.zh: 确实非常昂贵。

sentences.en: So, the wife of Bath is clearly quite a woman.
sentences.zh: 所以，巴斯妇人显然是个相当了不起的女人。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: And she tells a tremendous tale, which is about rape.
sentences.zh: 她讲了一个极为精彩的故事，内容关于强奸。

sentences.en: This is why the idea that Chaucer himself was a rapist is so unsettling.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么认为乔叟本人是个强奸犯的说法如此令人不安。

sentences.en: Because the wife of Bath is a very, very, I think it's not too anachronistic to use the word, a very feminist figure.
sentences.zh: 因为巴斯妇人是一个非常非常——我认为使用这个词并不过时——非常具有女权主义色彩的人物。

sentences.en: So, her story is about a knight who has committed a rape.
sentences.zh: 她的故事讲的是一个犯下强奸罪的骑士。

sentences.en: He's a rapiSt.
sentences.zh: 他是个强奸犯。

sentences.en: And he is threatened with execution.
sentences.zh: 他面临着被处决的威胁。

sentences.en: He's at the court of King Arthur.
sentences.zh: 他在亚瑟王的宫廷里。

sentences.en: But Gwynevere intervenes and says that if he can find out what it is that women most desire within a set period of time, then he will be spared execution.
sentences.zh: 但吉尼薇儿介入了，说如果他能在规定时间内查明女人内心最渴望的是什么，就可以免于一死。

sentences.en: And the knight kind of goes around trying to find it, can't find it.
sentences.zh: 于是这个骑士四处打听想找到答案，却找不到。

sentences.en: And then he meets a very ugly old woman who tells him the answer.
sentences.zh: 然后他遇到一个非常丑陋的老妇人，她告诉了他答案。

sentences.en: And the answer is that what women most desire is sovereignty over their husbands.
sentences.zh: 答案是，女人最渴望的是对她们丈夫的主导权。

sentences.en: And the price she demands for revealing this is that the knight will marry her.
sentences.zh: 她透露这个秘密所要求的代价是，骑士必须娶她。

sentences.en: And so, the knight thinks, oh, God, I've got to.
sentences.zh: 于是骑士心想，天哪，我只能答应了。

sentences.en: So, on their wedding night, they go to bed.
sentences.zh: 所以在他们的洞房花烛夜，他们上床了。

sentences.en: And the knight is appalled that he's in bed with this ugly old woman.
sentences.zh: 骑士对竟然跟这个丑陋的老妇人同床共枕感到震惊。

sentences.en: And she's very upset.
sentences.zh: 而她非常难过。

sentences.en: And she ends up offering him a choice.
sentences.zh: 最后她给了他一个选择。

sentences.en: She says that he can choose.
sentences.zh: 她说他可以自己选。

sentences.en: She has kind of magical powers.
sentences.zh: 她拥有某种魔法力量。

sentences.en: He can choose to have an old and ugly wife who will be true and loyal to him.
sentences.zh: 他可以选择一个年老丑陋但对他忠心耿耿的妻子。

sentences.en: So, in other words, she will remain as she is.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，她会保持原样。

sentences.en: Or she will change and become very, very beautiful, very youthful.
sentences.zh: 或者她会改变，变得非常非常美丽、非常年轻。

sentences.en: But she won't be faithful.
sentences.zh: 但她不会对忠诚。

sentences.en: So, which would he rather have?
sentences.zh: 那么他会选哪个呢？

sentences.en: And the knight kind of ponders it.
sentences.zh: 骑士仔细斟酌了一番。

sentences.en: And then he says, I can't decide.
sentences.zh: 然后他说，我决定不了。

sentences.en: You decide.
sentences.zh: 你来决定吧。

sentences.en: And his wife is so delighted that he has surrendered sovereignty to her that she allows him to have his cake and eat it.
sentences.zh: 他的妻子听到他把主导权交给了她，高兴极了，于是允许他鱼与熊掌兼得。

sentences.en: So, she turns into this kind of beautiful young woman.
sentences.zh: 所以，她变成了一个美丽迷人的年轻女子。

sentences.en: And she's very faithful.
sentences.zh: 而且她非常忠诚。

sentences.en: Oh, heartwarming.
sentences.zh: 哦，真是暖心。

sentences.en: So, there you go.
sentences.zh: 事情就是这样。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: So, this is the story that The Wife of Bath tells.
sentences.zh: 这就是巴斯妇人讲的故事。

sentences.en: But the thing that makes it one of the greatest, greatest pieces of writing in the whole of English is the prologue.
sentences.zh: 但让它成为整个英语文学中伟大的作品之一的，是它的序言。

sentences.en: So, the kind of the introduction to it where the wife of Bath speaks in her own voice at twice the length that she devotes to her story.
sentences.zh: 也就是引言部分，巴斯妇人用她自己的声音讲述，篇幅是她故事本身的整整两倍。

sentences.en: In here, she's telling the story of the five husbands that she's married.
sentences.zh: 在这里，她讲述了她嫁过的五个丈夫的故事。

sentences.en: And on the one hand, she's kind of cheerfully admitting all the tricks that she's employed to kind of bend them to her will.
sentences.zh: 一方面，她兴高采烈地承认了自己用来让他们顺从自己意愿的各种诡计。

sentences.en: But at the same time, she's describing the domestic abuse that several of them have inflicted on her.
sentences.zh: 但与此同时，她也在描述其中几个人对她施加的家庭暴力。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: So, who would suppose the woe that in my heart was and pain?
sentences.zh: “谁能料想我心中的悲伤与痛苦？”

sentences.en: So, you see into the kind of the depths of her misery when she's suffering abuse.
sentences.zh: 所以，当你看到她遭受虐待时，你能窥见她内心深渊般的痛苦。

sentences.en: But at the same time, she's very, very rebellious, witty, larger than life, celebrating sex, refusing to be cowed by the fact that she's kind of getting on in life.
sentences.zh: 但与此同时，她又非常非常叛逆、风趣、充满活力，赞美性爱，拒绝因年事已高而感到气馁。

sentences.en: And absolutely contemptuous of the arguments that men traditionally present, saying that women should be subordinate to men and that wives should be subordinate to husbands.
sentences.zh: 她极其鄙视传统男人提出的那些论调，即女人应该服从男人，妻子应该服从丈夫。

sentences.en: And she is kind of making the point, which is one that's absolute standard now in feminist theory, that men can write misogynist texts because they're men.
sentences.zh: 她提出了一个如今在女权主义理论中绝对标准的观点：男人之所以能写出厌女的文本，是因为他们是男人。

sentences.en: And because in the Middle Ages and back into late antiquity, her husbands are always quoting the church fathers.
sentences.zh: 而且因为在中世纪甚至追溯到古代晚期，她的丈夫们总是在引用教会神父的话。

sentences.en: And she's saying, well, they would say that, they're men.
sentences.zh: 而她则说，他们当然会这么说，因为他们是男人。

sentences.en: Yeah, of course.
sentences.zh: 对，当然。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: You know, if lions were writing it, they would write it about lions.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，如果是狮子在写，它们就会写关于狮子的内容。

sentences.en: And again, to quote Marion Turner, who wrote a wonderful biography of The Wife of Bath, she says of The Wife of Bath that she is the first ordinary woman in English literature.
sentences.zh: 再次引用马里昂·特纳的话，她写过一本精彩的《巴斯妇人》传记，她评价巴斯妇人是英国文学中的第一个普通女性。

sentences.en: By that, I mean the first mercantile, working, sexually active woman, not a virginal princess or queen, not a nun, a witch, not a damsel in distress,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，第一个经商的、工作的、有性生活的女性，而不是纯洁的公主或女王，不是修女、女巫，也不是落难的少女，

sentences.en: nor a functional servant character, not an allegory.
sentences.zh: 更不是功能性的仆人角色，不是某种寓言形象。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: But a living, breathing, flesh and blood woman with agency and with, you know, desires and anxieties and all these things of her own.
sentences.zh: 而是一个有血有肉、活生生的女人，她有自主权，有自己的欲望、焦虑以及所有这些东西。

sentences.en: I mean, she's basically Chaucer's full staff.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，她基本上就是福斯塔夫的乔叟版。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: And Marion Turner in her book suggests that actually she's a direct influence on full staff.
sentences.zh: 马里昂·特纳在书中暗示，实际上她是福斯塔夫的直接灵感来源。

sentences.en: So she is a literary figure, but like so much in Chaucer's poetry, she tells us a lot about what is convulsive about society in England in the wake of the Black Death.
sentences.zh: 所以她是一个文学形象，但就像乔叟诗歌中的许多东西一样，她向我们展示了黑死病之后英国社会的动荡之处。

sentences.en: So why is she a wife of Bath?
sentences.zh: 那么，她为什么叫巴斯妇人呢？

sentences.en: Well, Marion Turner in her book points out that there is a lot of cloth manufacturing going on around Bath.
sentences.zh: 马里昂·特纳在书中指出，巴斯周边有很多呢绒制造业。

sentences.en: Bath is near the Cotswolds, the wool trade, the booming kind of wool villages and towns.
sentences.zh: 巴斯靠近科茨沃尔德，那是羊毛贸易的中心，有着蓬勃发展的羊毛村庄和城镇。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: So, Tom, somebody listening to or reading the story in the 14th century, they would immediately say, oh, rich.
sentences.zh: 所以，汤姆，14世纪听到或读到这个故事的人，会立刻说，哦，真有钱。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: You know, an area where there's a lot of social and economic change.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，这是一个有着大量社会和经济变革的地区。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: It's kind of, you know, it's like she's a tech entrepreneur, I guess would be equivalent for us.
sentences.zh: 这就好像，你知道的，她就像是个科技创业者，我想对我们来说这就相当于这种感觉。

sentences.en: She's someone who is in a hot spot of the economy.
sentences.zh: 她是一个身处经济热潮中的人。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: And one that explains how she's as rich as she is.
sentences.zh: 这也解释了她为什么会这么有钱。

sentences.en: And it's not surprising that she's a woman, because what has also happened in the wake of the Black Death is that it has accentuated trends, not just within England,
sentences.zh: 她是个女性并不令人意外，因为黑死病之后发生的事情，不仅加剧了英国的趋势，

sentences.en: but across much of Northern Europe, say Flanders as well, and Germany and Scandinavia, in which women can increasingly choose who they want to marry.
sentences.zh: 而且在整个北欧也是如此，比如法兰德斯、德国和斯堪的纳维亚，女性越来越多地能够自主选择嫁给谁。

sentences.en: They're maybe having fewer children compared, say, to women in the Mediterranean, and they can marry repeatedly.
sentences.zh: 与地中海地区的女性相比，她们可能生孩子较少，并且可以多次结婚。

sentences.en: And this gains some capital, which they can then kind of invest in things like, say, cloth manufacturer.
sentences.zh: 这让她们积攒了一些资本，然后她们可以把这些资本投资到诸如呢绒制造之类的行业中。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: And probably more women are involved in the economy in this period, in England, in the Netherlands, whatever, in the lowlands, than anywhere else in the world.
sentences.zh: 在这个时期，英国、荷兰等低地国家的女性参与经济的比例可能比世界上任何其他地方都要高。

sentences.en: They probably are exercising higher standards of numeracy, higher standards of literacy.
sentences.zh: 她们可能拥有更高的算术水平和识字水平。

sentences.en: So again, to quote Marion Turner, there is widespread agreement that in the second half of the 14th century,
sentences.zh: 所以，再次引用马里昂·特纳的话，人们普遍认为，在14世纪下半叶，

sentences.en: many English women had more choices and more autonomy than they had at other points in history or in other places.
sentences.zh: 许多英国女性拥有比历史上其他时期或其它地方更多的选择和自主权。

sentences.en: So the wife of Bath, you know, her feminism is something that Chaucer is not inventing.
sentences.zh: 因此，巴斯妇人的女权主义并不是乔叟凭空捏造的。

sentences.en: Clearly, he recognizes that it's an expression of something that is distinctive about the society in which he's living.
sentences.zh: 很明显，他意识到这是他所生活的社会独特面貌的一种表现。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: And the whole emphasis on the wife of Bath, you know, she's a serial person who's marrying.
sentences.zh: 而且关于巴斯妇人的整体强调，你知道的，她是一个不断结婚的连续婚姻者。

sentences.en: This is a trend in England at this time.
sentences.zh: 这是当时英国的一种趋势。

sentences.en: The idea that widows marry is very, very disapproved by the church fathers.
sentences.zh: 寡妇再婚的想法是教会神父们非常非常不赞成的。

sentences.en: And this is what the wife of Bath is always, you know, complaining about.
sentences.zh: 这也是巴斯妇人一直在抱怨的事情。

sentences.en: She's all in favor of it.
sentences.zh: 她完全赞成这一点。

sentences.en: And just as the church fathers cite scripture saying it's a sin, she cites and often misquotes scripture to say it's absolutely brilliant, absolutely fine.
sentences.zh: 正如教会神父引经据典说这是一种罪过一样，她也引用并经常错误引用经文来说这绝对棒极了，完全没问题。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: And what women can do in this period is that they marry very young.
sentences.zh: 在这个时期，女性可以做的是她们结婚很早。

sentences.en: So 12 is, you know, is when you basically, as a girl, you kind of enter the marriage economy and girls will often be married to husbands who are much older than them.
sentences.zh: 所以12岁时，作为一个女孩，你基本上就进入了婚姻市场，女孩们通常会嫁给比她们大得多的丈夫。

sentences.en: So the Merchant's Tale also is about this.
sentences.zh: 所以《商人的故事》讲的也是这个。

sentences.en: It's about a very elderly man marrying a very young girl.
sentences.zh: 讲的是一个极老的老头娶了一个极年轻的女孩。

sentences.en: And that means the husbands die.
sentences.zh: 这意味着丈夫们会去世。

sentences.en: The girl, she can be quite young.
sentences.zh: 而女孩还很年轻。

sentences.en: She pockets a lot of the inheritance.
sentences.zh: 她能捞到一大笔遗产。

sentences.en: So under the common law, widow can keep a third of the husband's property for life.
sentences.zh: 根据普通法，寡妇可以终身保留丈夫三分之一的财产。

sentences.en: And if you're, you know, your husband's dead when you're 18, you marry again, he dies, you know, you're 25.
sentences.zh: 如果你在18岁时丈夫就死了，你再婚，他又死了，你25岁。

sentences.en: And so it goes on.
sentences.zh: 情况就是这样继续下去。

sentences.en: You can accrue quite a lot of property.
sentences.zh: 你可以积累相当多的财产。

sentences.en: So you build your fortune.
sentences.zh: 所以你积累了财富。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: And this is particularly true of women who are involved in trade.
sentences.zh: 对于参与经商的女性来说尤其如此。

sentences.en: So in London, a widow inherits the marital home for life.
sentences.zh: 在伦敦，寡妇可以终身继承婚房。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: That's not the case under the common law, but it is for merchants in London.
sentences.zh: 根据普通法并非如此，但对伦敦的商人来说是这样的。

sentences.en: And in London, a widow can keep a third of all the kind of the movable goods that a husband has, again, for life.
sentences.zh: 在伦敦，寡妇同样可以终身保留丈夫所有动产的三分之一。

sentences.en: So, you know, it's possible for women to end up very, very wealthy.
sentences.zh: 所以，女性最终变得非常非常富有是完全可能的。

sentences.en: And the wife of Bath is, in that sense, the embodiment of that cultural trend.
sentences.zh: 从这个意义上说，巴斯妇人就是这种文化趋势的化身。

sentences.en: And there is a real life example that parallels the wife of Bath that illustrates just how wealthy a woman could become by remarrying.
sentences.zh: 有一个与巴斯妇人平行的真实生活范例，它说明了通过再婚女性可以变得多么富有。

sentences.en: And that is none other than Chaucer's own granddaughter.
sentences.zh: 而这个人不是别人，正是乔叟自己的孙女。

sentences.en: That's Alice, right?
sentences.zh: 那是爱丽丝，对吧？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So Chaucer dies in 1400, shortly after Henry IV has come to the throne.
sentences.zh: 乔叟于1400年去世，就在亨利四世登基后不久。

sentences.en: And, of course, Chaucer is, you know, he's been a loyal associate of John of Gaunt.
sentences.zh: 当然，乔叟一直是冈特的约翰的忠实同伴。

sentences.en: So he survived Richard II's reign.
sentences.zh: 所以他在理查二世的统治下存活了下来。

sentences.en: And now that Henry has become king, probably the last poem that Chaucer writes is a poem asking him for a bit of money.
sentences.zh: 现在亨利成了国王，乔叟写的最后一首诗可能就是一首向他要点钱的诗。

sentences.en: You know, he's kind of, he's done amazingly well for a person of his social background, but not as well as his granddaughter Alice does.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，以他的社会背景来说，他过得相当不错，但还不如他的孙女爱丽丝过得好。

sentences.en: So by the age of 24, she's twice widowed and both of them have left her with a lot of money.
sentences.zh: 所以到24岁时，她已经两次丧偶，而这两任丈夫都给她留下了巨额财产。

sentences.en: And she then goes on to marry William de la Pole, who will in due course become the Duke of Suffolk and who is the grandson of the Michael de la Pole,
sentences.zh: 然后她嫁给了威廉·德·拉·波尔，他后来成为了萨福克公爵，同时他也是迈克尔·德·拉·波尔的孙子，

sentences.en: who was the chancellor under Richard II and got attainted.
sentences.zh: 后者曾是理查二世时期的的大法官，并被判叛国剥夺爵位。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Who we talked about last time.
sentences.zh: 也就是我们上次聊过的那个人。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: So the Duke of Suffolk himself, the one that Alice has married, he also gets attainted and actually gets executed.
sentences.zh: 所以萨福克公爵本人，也就是爱丽丝嫁的那位，他也遭到了剥夺爵位并最终被处决。

sentences.en: But Alice keeps hold of all his, his lands and property and she remains a widow for 25 years and she speculates and she increases her wealth.
sentences.zh: 但爱丽丝保住了他所有的土地和财产，她守寡了25年，通过投机让自己的财富不断增值。

sentences.en: And she basically becomes, I mean, one of the richest people in the whole kingdom, hugely respected, massive, massive kind of operator.
sentences.zh: 她基本上成为了，我的意思是，整个王国最富有的人之一，备受尊敬，是个极其厉害的人物。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: And amazingly, her son, John de la Pole ends up marrying Elizabeth of York, who is the younger sister of Edward IV and Richard III.
sentences.zh: 令人叫绝的是，她的儿子约翰·德·拉·波尔最终娶了约克的伊丽莎白，后者是爱德华四世和理查三世的亲妹妹。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: So she is the aunt of the princes in the tower.
sentences.zh: 所以她是塔中王子的阿姨。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: And she has a son.
sentences.zh: 而她有一个儿子。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And her son, Tom.
sentences.zh: 还有她的儿子汤姆。

sentences.en: So the son of Elizabeth of York and John de la Pole.
sentences.zh: 也就是约克的伊丽莎白和约翰·德·拉·波尔的儿子。

sentences.en: This is very confusing.
sentences.zh: 这太让人糊涂了。

sentences.en: That would make him Chaucer's great, great grandson.
sentences.zh: 那他岂不是乔叟的玄孙了。

sentences.en: He's also called John de la Pole.
sentences.zh: 他也叫约翰·德·拉·波尔。

sentences.en: He is.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: And he becomes the heir to Richard III.
sentences.zh: 而且他成了理查三世的继承人。

sentences.en: So in 1484, Richard III names this John de la Pole, Chaucer's great, great grandson, as his heir, which is incredible.
sentences.zh: 所以在1484年，理查三世指定这个约翰·德·拉·波尔——也就是乔叟的玄孙——为他的继承人，这简直难以置信。

sentences.en: And of course, Richard III gets defeated by Henry VII, who marries Elizabeth of York's niece, also called Elizabeth, very confusing.
sentences.zh: 当然，理查三世后来被亨利七世击败了，而亨利七世娶了约克的伊丽莎白的侄女，也叫伊丽莎白，非常令人头大。

sentences.en: And John de la Pole never ends up becoming king, but he's still very much on the scene.
sentences.zh: 约翰·德·拉·波尔最终没有当上国王，但他依然十分活跃。

sentences.en: And two years after the Battle of Bosworth in 1487, Lambert Simnel, raising the banner of rebellion, John de la Pole is there and he dies at the Battle of Stoke,
sentences.zh: 在博斯沃思战役两年后的1487年，兰伯特·西姆内尔举起了叛乱的旗帜，约翰·德·拉·波尔也在其中，他在斯托克战役中阵亡了，

sentences.en: which Henry VII wins against Lambert Simnel.
sentences.zh: 那是亨利七世击败兰伯特·西姆内尔的战役。

sentences.en: But I mean, amazing, amazing that Chaucer's heirs are that close to the throne.
sentences.zh: 但我的意思是，乔叟的后代竟然离王位这么近，真的太不可思议了。

sentences.en: So Chaucer's great, great grandson could have been king.
sentences.zh: 所以乔叟的玄孙本来是有机会当国王的。

sentences.en: Could have been king.
sentences.zh: 本来有机会当国王的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Crikey.
sentences.zh: 天哪。

sentences.en: That's not bad for...
sentences.zh: 这对于……

sentences.en: What was Chaucer, the great grandson or something of a...
sentences.zh: 乔叟算是什么来头，是某个……的曾孙吗？

sentences.en: Of a pub landlord, of Al Murray.
sentences.zh: 某个酒吧老板的，就像阿尔·默里那样。

sentences.en: That's amazing.
sentences.zh: 太神奇了。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: So I think that, I mean, Chaucer's life is fascinating as an illustration of the social turbulence of the age and of just how far people could rise.
sentences.zh: 所以我觉得，乔叟的一生作为那个时代社会动荡以及人们阶层跃升极限的写照，实在太迷人了。

sentences.en: And it's not surprising that Chaucer himself, who's so socially mobile, should have been so interested in that as a theme.
sentences.zh: 难怪乔叟本人身处如此剧烈的社会流动之中，会对这个主题产生这么浓厚的兴趣。

sentences.en: And of course, there's a sense in which that aspect of him gets buried because he very rapidly becomes, you know, the father of English literature, this great patriarchal figure.
sentences.zh: 当然，在某种意义上，他这一面被掩盖了，因为他很快就变成了，你知道的，英国文学之父，这样一位伟大的宗师级人物。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: The Canterbury Tales gets famously printed by Caxton, one of the first books to be printed in England.
sentences.zh: 《坎特伯雷故事集》因凯克斯顿的印刷而闻名遐迩，这也是英国最早印刷的书籍之一。

sentences.en: He's the first English writer to have a complete works.
sentences.zh: 他是第一位拥有全集的英国作家。

sentences.en: So that happens in Henry VIII.
sentences.zh: 所以那是在亨利八世统治时期发生的。

sentences.en: And then the end of the 16th century, his tomb...
sentences.zh: 然后到了16世纪末，他的墓……

sentences.en: So he's not buried in Westminster Abbey because he's a poet.
sentences.zh: 他安葬在威斯敏斯特教堂并不是因为他是个诗人。

sentences.en: He's buried in Westminster Abbey as a mark of respect from the monks who he associated with.
sentences.zh: 他安葬在威斯敏斯特教堂，是为了表示与他交往过的修士们的敬意。

sentences.en: Oh, right.
sentences.zh: 哦，原来如此。

sentences.en: But he gets put in a kind of improved tomb that suits his stature as the father of English literature.
sentences.zh: 但他被安置在一个升级版的墓穴里，这符合他作为英国文学之父的地位。

sentences.en: And Tom, we did say we're not the rest is literature.
sentences.zh: 汤姆，我们说过我们讲的不是“其余皆是历史”。

sentences.en: But he is the father of English literature, isn't he?
sentences.zh: 但他确实是英国文学之父，对吧？

sentences.en: Because it's not just what he does with the language, inventing all these words and phrases that we are so familiar with today.
sentences.zh: 因为这不仅在于他对语言的运用，创造了那么多我们今天耳熟能详的词汇和短语。

sentences.en: But he creates a way of writing, which, as you said, is panoramic, is often very funny, is earthy, is sort of rooted in the concrete everyday realities of English life.
sentences.zh: 还在于他创造了一种写作方式，正如你所说，具有全景式视角，往往非常风趣，质朴接地气，根植于英国生活的具体日常现实中。

sentences.en: That so many writers, I mean, Shakespeare and Dickens would be two obvious examples, have kind of picked up.
sentences.zh: 以至于许多作家——莎士比亚和狄更斯就是两个明显的例子——都从中汲取了养分。

sentences.en: But, yeah, I mean, I'm not saying it's impossible that they would have done what they did without Chaucer, but Chaucer absolutely stands at the centre of that tradition,
sentences.zh: 但是，是的，我的意思是，我并不是说如果没有乔叟他们就绝对写不出那样的作品，但乔叟绝对处于那个传统的中心，

sentences.en: doesn't he?
sentences.zh: 不是吗？

sentences.en: He does.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: And I think his achievement is so great that it legitimises for his literary heirs the idea that writing in English can be as prestigious as writing in Latin or French.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为他的成就是如此伟大，以至于他向他的文学后继者们证明了一个道理：用英语写作可以和用拉丁语或法语写作一样享有崇高的地位。

sentences.en: So, you know, all the great poetry of the 16th and 17th centuries would kind of be unthinkable, really, without Chaucer's inspiration.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道的，16世纪和17世纪的所有伟大诗歌，如果没有乔叟的启发，简直是不可想象的。

sentences.en: And the other, I mean, purely literary way in which Chaucer is massively influential is that because he's writing in the London dialect,
sentences.zh: 另一个纯粹从文学角度来看，乔叟产生巨大影响的原因是，因为他使用的是伦敦方言，

sentences.en: it cements the sense of Southeastern English as being, I mean, not received pronunciation,
sentences.zh: 这巩固了东南部英语的地位，虽然还不是公认发音（RP），

sentences.en: but being the kind of the model that various other English dialects will start to be shaped by over the course of the 15th and 16th centuries.
sentences.zh: 但它成为了在15世纪和16世纪期间，开始塑造其他各种英国方言的某种模范标准。

sentences.en: And so, purely as a literary figure, I mean, he's the first great writer of the language that has become the global lingua franca.
sentences.zh: 因此，仅作为一个文学人物，我的意思是，他是那个已经成为全球通用语的语言的第一位伟大作家。

sentences.en: And he's a poet who, I mean, I know we've kind of made a joke about how he's impossible to understand, but actually he's not that hard to understand.
sentences.zh: 他也是一位诗人，我知道我们曾开玩笑说他多么难以理解，但实际上他并没有那么难懂。

sentences.en: If you may, you know, he doesn't take that much of an effort.
sentences.zh: 如果你愿意的话，你知道的，他其实不需要费那么大劲。

sentences.en: And he is a great, great poet whose achievements, as I said, I found them, you know, they gave me kind of great comfort and distraction in the first weeks of the lockdown.
sentences.zh: 他是一位伟大的、真正的诗人，正如我所说，他的成就在封锁的第一周里给我带来了巨大的慰藉和消遣。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: So I'm very happy to have done him.
sentences.zh: 所以我很高兴能讲他。

sentences.en: But I think you can also justify doing an episode of The Rest is History on Chaucer because he's so fascinating as a window onto the events that we've been describing.
sentences.zh: 但我也觉得，做一期关于乔叟的《历史大不同》节目是完全合情合理的，因为作为一扇窥探我们刚才所描述那些事件的窗户，他实在太迷人了。

sentences.en: All right.
sentences.zh: 好嘞。

sentences.en: Brilliant.
sentences.zh: 太精彩了。

sentences.en: Well, thank you, Tom.
sentences.zh: 那么，谢谢你，汤姆。

sentences.en: It was not just a tour de force, actually, it was a tour d'horizon of medieval England.
sentences.zh: 这不仅是一次才华横溢的展示，实际上，这是一次对中世纪英格兰的纵览。

sentences.en: Now, the good news for listeners who've enjoyed this is that we are going to pause now, as we often like to do, but we will be returning later in the year, won't we,
sentences.zh: 现在，对于喜欢这一期的听众来说，好消息是我们要像往常一样暂停一下，但我们会在今年晚些时候回归，对吧，

sentences.en: to this period.
sentences.zh: 继续这个时期。

sentences.en: And you'll be taking up the story of what happens next.
sentences.zh: 你将接着讲述接下来发生的故事。

sentences.en: Henry IV, parts one and two.
sentences.zh: 《亨利四世》上下篇。

sentences.en: And Henry V, then Agincourt, and one of the most evil characters in history, Joan of Arc, will be making her debut on The Rest is History.
sentences.zh: 还有《亨利五世》，接着是阿让库尔战役，以及历史上最邪恶的角色之一——圣女贞德，也将首次亮相《历史大不同》。

sentences.en: And the good news for those of you who didn't enjoy this is that actually next week we'll be doing something different.
sentences.zh: 而对于那些不喜欢这一期的听众，好消息是实际上我们下周会做点别的内容。

sentences.en: But I don't believe such people exist, Tom, because everybody will have enjoyed this.
sentences.zh: 但我才不信会有这种人呢，汤姆，因为每个人都会喜欢这一期的。

sentences.en: There will definitely be no Middle English in the next episode.
sentences.zh: 下一期节目绝对不会出现中古英语。

sentences.en: Oh, that is disappointing.
sentences.zh: 哦，那太让人失望了。

sentences.en: So on that bombshell, thank you very much, Tom.
sentences.zh: 带着这个重磅消息，非常感谢你，汤姆。

sentences.en: Thank you, everybody.
sentences.zh: 谢谢大家。

sentences.en: And we'll see you next week.
sentences.zh: 我们下周见。

sentences.en: Bye-bye.
sentences.zh: 拜拜。

sentences.zh: 拜拜。
